Give the commit path a scope model

A claim is about a scope; the tool only ever saw one invocation. When those
differed it had no way to tell, so an honest "all 150 tests pass" got flagged
whenever claim-check's own run happened to be narrower. That was the single
likeliest reason to uninstall this.

The information was already there and being thrown away. RunResult now
reports the argv, cwd and command it actually used, evidence.scope_of_run
turns that into a scope descriptor, and compare_claims takes it as an
argument so the decision stays in the one file that owns policy.

A narrowed run no longer contradicts a claim it cannot cover, and just as
importantly no longer confirms one. `pytest -k test_a` on a file whose
test_b fails reports "1 passed, 1 deselected", which makes "all tests pass"
true of what ran while the suite is red. Agreeing there would launder a false
claim into a verified one.

Runs that were not narrowed are judged exactly as strictly as before, so
"all 22 tests pass" against a real 21 is still caught. Abstention keys off
positively detected narrowing, never off arithmetic.

cli.py's verdict dispatch ended in a fall-through `return 1`, which would
have turned every abstention into a block. Changed to an explicit blocking
allowlist before the new status existed.

Declared commands get the opposite bias from observed ones. An unrecognised
runner in `--command "hatch run test"` must not read as narrowed, or every
hatch and make user silently gets zero verification forever.

The two tests that pinned these limitations now assert the fix, and both
check the reason rather than the exit code, since abstaining and agreeing
are indistinguishable from a 0.

370 passed.
